newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday in dull trading led by a strong rise in unlinked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.17 pct to 101.56
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 pct to 100.94.
Volume was very low at 93 million shekels and traders said investors showed little interest in the bond market.
"Investors are now more interested in the stock market and activity is falling," said Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Securities.
"The market is very quiet. There is simply no new information to move the market," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
Traders said CPI-linked bonds were mixed, closing only slightly higher.
"The Makam is continuing to rise but yields have fallen sharply to 13.87 percent, which is not attractive at all," Rosenfeld said.
"The only logical explanation for the rise of the Makam is expectations that the central bank will raise the reserve requirement," the First International trader said.

Financial sources said last week that the Bank of Israel may raise the reserve requirement by five percentage points for commercial banks in an effort to combat growing liquidity in the economy. That would raise the requirement to between eight and 11 percent, depending on the term of the deposit.
"Unlinked bonds rose sharply closing the yields difference with Makam's (which are also unlinked)," the First International trader added.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds closed higher following the recent rally of the American currency against the German mark.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
